/days-out: Big days out. Little discoveries. Plenty to smile about.

Right, where are we off to? A big ride, a wander by the sea, somewhere brilliant for lunch — there is plenty to build a UK day out around. Start with the bit everyone is excited about, then leave room for the little discoveries. /seaside: Sea air, chips and a proper day out

There is something about the seaside, isn't there? The first glimpse of the water, the smell of chips and somebody already asking for an ice cream. UK seaside days out can be a beach wander, a pier visit or a whole weekend of discoveries. Browse Blackpool, Skegness and Great Yarmouth, then put your own day together with food stops, attractions and places to stay nearby. The arcades are there when you fancy a game, too. Take your time — you have come out to enjoy yourselves.
/food-and-drink: Good food. Full bellies. Happy days.

Now we are talking. A bag of chips by the sea, a proper pub lunch or a curry worth making a stop for — good food is part of the adventure. These UK food and drink guides help you find a restaurant, café or takeaway that fits your day, then see what else is nearby. Start with Masala & Malt in Grimsby, Reel Plaice in Ayr or the food stops around your chosen town. Open the individual guide for the story and practical details. Nobody wants the best bit of the day to be a soggy sandwich in the car.
/places-to-stay: One more day? Make a night of it.

Just when you are getting into the swing of it, somebody says it is time to go home. How about staying a little longer? These UK hotel and accommodation guides help you choose a base for a seaside break, a town visit or a weekend with a big attraction in the middle. Browse places to stay in Blackpool and beyond, have a look at the food and days-out guides nearby, then check the room and dates that suit you. A good base leaves more time for the evening wander, the meal and tomorrow's discoveries.
/attractions: Big rides, big grins and a day to remember

This is the bit everyone has been waiting for. A theme park, a zoo, a castle, a museum — pick the UK attraction that gets your lot excited and build the day around it. Browse the categories, open a venue guide and see what you fancy. Add somewhere to eat and, if it is a bigger trip, a place to stay nearby. Leave enough time to enjoy the main event. /theme-parks: Hands up. Here comes the big drop.

That first climb, the little pause at the top and then — here we go! UK theme parks give you plenty to get excited about, from big coasters to family rides and a gentler first adventure. Browse the park guides, check which rides suit your group and choose the day you want. Alton Towers, Thorpe Park and Blackpool Pleasure Beach are among the places to explore. Sort the tickets and the journey, then save your energy for the rides. There is a lot of fun to get through.
/family-fun: A day out the whole gang can get into

Getting everyone excited about the same plan can take a bit of doing. Start with something the children will enjoy, add a food stop and leave space for a little wandering. These UK family days-out guides bring together attractions, activities and places to explore. Open the individual guide to see who it suits and what you need to know before you set off. Big smiles, tired legs and a good story on the way home — that is a day well spent.
/zoos: Somebody will have a favourite before you even get through the gate. UK zoos and wildlife parks make a day of watching, wondering and spotting something you have never seen up close. Browse the guides and see which place gets your group talking. Give yourselves time to explore, check the day's talks or activities with the venue and work a food break into the plan. The best bits are often the ones you stop and watch for a little longer.
/sea-life: Big eyes, strange creatures and a splash of wonder

There is a whole world going on under the water. UK aquariums and sea-life attractions are full of things to stop, stare at and talk about afterwards. Browse the venue guides, pick a place that fits your trip and give yourselves time to enjoy it. If you are heading to the coast, add a promenade wander or somewhere for lunch nearby. An indoor sea-life visit can make a lovely part of the day when the weather has other ideas.
/museums: You go in for a look round and suddenly there is something you cannot stop talking about. UK museums and galleries have all sorts to explore, from local stories and unusual collections to art that makes you stop in your tracks. Browse the guides and choose a subject your group will get into. Check the exhibition or activity you fancy, leave time for a proper look and find somewhere nearby for a drink afterwards. There is plenty to discover here.
/historical-sites: Old places with a cracking story to tell

Castles, grand houses, ruins and the places that make you wonder what life was like back then. UK historic attractions turn a day out into a bit of an adventure. Browse the guides and see which story catches your eye. Think about how much walking you fancy, check the current opening arrangements and leave time to explore properly. Add a food stop or a wander in the nearby town and you have the makings of a lovely day.
/beaches: Bucket, spade and a little bit of freedom

That feeling when the shoes come off and the beach opens up in front of you — lovely. UK beach days can be sandcastles, a walk along the water or just finding a spot to sit and watch the world go by. Browse the guides, choose a beach that suits your group and look at what is nearby for food or another stop. Check the weather, tide and local signs before heading down. Then let the day find its own pace.
/piers: A little further out. A lot to look around.

A walk along a seaside pier has its own little rhythm. Stop for the view, see what is open, have a look at the amusements and find something to eat when you fancy it. Add the beach, the town or another attraction nearby and make a proper outing of it.
/outdoors: Fresh air, muddy boots and a proper breather

Get outside and give the day a bit of room. A waterside wander, a park, a garden or somewhere green to stretch your legs — UK outdoor days out can be as lively or as relaxed as you fancy. Browse the guides, choose a place that suits your group and leave time to enjoy the stops along the way. Pack for the weather and think about the route before you set off. A café at the end is a very decent finishing touch.
/hidden-gems: Well, look at that. A new favourite waiting to happen.

The little place you nearly walked past can turn into the bit you remember most. These UK hidden-gem guides are for the unusual stops, quieter discoveries and places that deserve a closer look. /bowling: One good bowl and suddenly everyone is competitive

Browse the venue guides, choose your session and check the arrangements for your group. Add a meal nearby if you fancy making more of it. There is always time for a bit of friendly scorekeeping — and somebody will be telling you about their best bowl afterwards.
/cinemas: A big screen and a proper switch-off

Browse the cinema guides, then check the venue's current listings and screening times for the film you want. Find somewhere nearby for food before or afterwards and make a little occasion of it. Sometimes a couple of hours with a good story is exactly what you fancy.
/holiday-parks: Unpack once. Enjoy a little longer.
